intended_application: Semiconductor Production Scheduling and Disruption Management: support interpretation of disruption information, coordination, and preparation of recovery options for human review; no autonomous production-schedule changes.
organization: Hypothetical large semiconductor wafer fabrication company operating multiple production lines; no real company or observed deployment is represented.
business_need: Hypothetical objectives [H2]: improve production-disruption response, reduce manual coordination, and support recovery planning. No realized performance improvement, ROI, or pilot outcome is supplied.
users_stakeholders: Hypothetical stakeholders [H1]: production planners, line operations, process and quality engineers, maintenance coordinators, MES/ERP administrators, information security, and manufacturing management.
capabilities_constraints: Hypothetical premises [H1]: existing MES and ERP systems and multiple production lines. Proposed access, data freshness/quality, manufacturing-constraint coverage, interfaces, cybersecurity controls, staffing, budget, and review capacity are unverified. Human-in-the-Loop governance: authorized personnel must review and approve consequential schedule changes; the proposed agent may prepare options but may not commit changes. No integration or effective supervision has been demonstrated.
risk_consequence_context: Hypothetical consequence context [H1]: erroneous recovery options or missed constraints could contribute to production disruption, operational/financial losses, and manufacturing-quality risks if acted upon. Likelihood and magnitude are unknown. Human approval is a stipulated authority boundary, not proof that errors will be detected. No incidents or quantified losses are asserted.
management_question: Should a large semiconductor manufacturing company initiate a six-month, human-in-the-loop Agentic AI pilot for production scheduling and disruption management, and under what evidence, operational constraints, and governance conditions should it consider expanding deployment?
time_horizon: Decision now on a proposed six-month controlled pilot; expansion is a separate later decision conditional on evidence, with no automatic authorization.
additional_context:
SHARED TECHNOLOGY DEFINITION
Agentic AI means a bounded class of integrated, model-directed systems that select tool-mediated actions and use environmental feedback to pursue delegated goals within permissions and human oversight.
This is the same technology class in both cases; neither the organization nor the proposed integration changes its definition.

CASE-SPECIFIC PREMISES
[H1] All organization, stakeholder, infrastructure, governance, and consequence details in this case are stipulated hypothetical premises. Existing MES/ERP does not imply available interfaces or validated agent integration. Any pilot would require approved access and constraints, authorized human decisions, and a fallback process; these are proposed prerequisites, not verified controls. [H2] Disruption-response, coordination, and recovery benefits are objectives only. Baseline methods, actual constraints, costs, data readiness, oversight workload, and expansion thresholds have not been supplied. Assess this decision without manufacturing results.

EVIDENCE SCOPE NOTE
The unchanged approved payload below contains an [H1/H2] summary of the original semiconductor scenario. That line is a record of the primary scenario, not shared external evidence. Only the current case fields and CASE-SPECIFIC PREMISES above define H1/H2 for this run. Do not import manufacturer premises into a professional-services case. C1-C5 and the shared technology definition are identical across cases. Neither case supplies comparative evidence establishing uniquely new capabilities over traditional automation, rule-based workflows, or optimization systems; do not invent those comparisons or preassign a classification.
